answer: In a market where agents trade saffron, each voting identity must lock 100 tokens in a vault for 30 days, and voting power is proportional to locked stake. Splitting one balance among fake identities creates no extra power: an attacker seeking 10% of the vote must still immobilize 10% of all voting stake. The cost is capital tied up for a month and its forgone yield, so a ripple of new accounts cannot cheaply multiply influence.
